title: Window-Aware Scheduling for Health Messaging under Platform Delivery Constraints: Evidence from an AI-Powered WhatsApp Maternal and Infant Health Chatbot in Nigeria
abstract: arXiv:2611.02834v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: WhatsApp lets a business send free-form messages only within 24 hours of a user's last message; outside this customer service window, only pre-approved templates are delivered. Health chatbots inherit this rule, but its cost is rarely measured. We analyse 98,607 messages sent to 3,696 mothers by a WhatsApp maternal health chatbot in Nigeria, with a largely separate export as replication. No free-form message failed with the window open (0 of 35,500), and failure jumped by 93.0 percentage points (95% CI 87.0 to 99.1) at exactly 24 hours. Two flows produced 66.1% of failures, including an offer to speak with a medical professional that, as built, reached 0.3 in 100 mothers whose window had closed. We formalise window-aware scheduling as a decision problem with an action of known zero value. Model-based offline evaluation, with bounds for unconfirmed delivery, estimates that sending the offer as an approved template would reach 81.5 to 86.8

translated_title: 平台投递约束下健康消息传递的窗口感知调度：来自尼日利亚AI驱动的WhatsApp孕产妇与婴幼儿健康聊天机器人的证据
translated_abstract: WhatsApp仅允许企业在用户最后一条消息后的24小时内发送自由格式的消息；在此客户服务窗口之外，只能发送预先批准的模板消息。健康聊天机器人继承了这一规则，但其造成的成本却很少被测量。我们分析了尼日利亚一个WhatsApp孕产妇健康聊天机器人发送给3,696位母亲的98,607条消息，并使用一个基本独立的数据导出作为复现验证。在窗口开启时，没有任何自由格式消息发送失败（35,500条中0条失败），而在恰好24小时处，失败率跃升了93.0个百分点（95%置信区间：87.0至99.1）。两个消息流程产生了66.1%的失败，其中包括一项“与医疗专业人员交谈”的服务提议——按原设计构建，在窗口已关闭的母亲中，每100位仅有0.3位能收到该提议。我们将窗口感知调度形式化为一个决策问题，其中包含一个已知价值为零的动作。基于模型的离线评估（对未确认送达的情况设定界限）估计，若将该提议作为已批准的模板发送，其送达率将达到81.5至86.8（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该研究首次量化了WhatsApp 24小时客户服务窗口对健康聊天机器人消息送达造成的损失，并将窗口感知调度形式化为决策问题，发现将关键医疗咨询服务以预批准模板发送可将送达率从几乎为零提升至约81.5%–86.8%。
en_tdlr: This study quantifies for the first time the delivery losses caused by WhatsApp's 24-hour customer service window for a maternal health chatbot, formalises window-aware scheduling as a decision problem, and shows that sending key health-service offers as pre-approved templates could raise reach from nearly zero to 81.5–86.8 per 100 mothers.
